import sys, json, uuid, hashlib, datetime

# THE ONE WRITER OF THE WALL (curator, GH #888). Everything that enters the
# window of the model behind this hive passes through here first and becomes
# ledger rows: a turn of the running round (`in_curate`), the model's own final
# answer (`in_llm`, the tap), a durable system slot (`in_slots` from the
# collector, `in_pack` from the identity pusher), a section of the model's
# sidecar block (`in_section`: `marks`), a pin of another hive (`in_pin`:
# `pins`), a gap's find `./push` kept for the round it opens (`in_addendum`,
# GH #895). Nothing here builds a window or calls a model -- that is `./policy`,
# and `./writer` hands episodes on.
#
# Every lane runs the same two steps against `./ledger`:
#   A  park the payload in `state` (key `pending:<id>`) and read, in ONE bundle,
#      what is already there -- the payload comes back in the same answer, so
#      nothing large rides in a context key;
#   B  write only what is new (blocks by hash, wall rows by
#      (session_id, turn_id, hash, nth), slots by path) and hand on.
# The store has no unique constraint (a core defer of the cell type), so "insert
# or nothing" is this read-before-write, and this cell runs `resident`: one
# child, strictly serial, so no second message of this cell reads between an A
# and its B -- and the RAM sets below catch the one gap left (two messages of
# the same round whose A answers both arrive before either B).
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc.get("body") or {}
envelope = doc.get("envelope") or {}
P = doc.get("params") or {}
header = envelope.get("header") or {}
hop = header.get("hop") or {}
ctx = header.get("context") or {}


# THE AUDIENCE GATE (GH #925). Every row of `wall`, `calls`, `marks`,
# `summaries` and `pins` carries the audience of the round that caused it
# (`audience_set`, a canonical JSON array), and a reader hands a row to a round
# iff the row has one and it names `*` or holds the round as a subset -- the
# affinity rule (templates/affinity/README.md, GH #154/#306). The round is
# `context.audience_set` of the message being served: this hive's edges set
# and delete only `cur_*`, so it rides the context through every ledger round
# trip exactly like `cur_origin`, and it is never guessed from a row. These
# functions are the same text in every cell of this hive that writes or reads
# rows; a lock holds them to one table. Every ledger read asks the store
# first (`round_where`, GH #932), so a hidden row never comes back at all; the
# Python gate stays as the second line behind it.


def audience_of(value):
    """An audience in its canonical form -- a JSON array of strings, sorted,
    no duplicates, no whitespace -- or None when there is none. The round
    arrives as TEXT (a JSON array in a string) and a column comes back as
    text; a list is taken as it is. Absent, empty text, a scalar or
    unparsable text is NOT DECLARED: the empty list is a declared round, None
    is no round at all (affinity `as_set`, GH #306)."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if not value.strip():
            return None
        try:
            value = json.loads(value)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    if not isinstance(value, list):
        return None
    return json.dumps(sorted({str(x) for x in value if str(x)}), separators=(",", ":"))


def allowed(round_value, origin):
    """The gate: a row whose audience is `origin` may reach the round
    `round_value` iff both are declared and the origin names `*` or holds the
    round as a subset. A row from before the rule has no origin and never
    leaves (OR-BD-5); a round nobody declared passes nothing."""
    r, o = audience_of(round_value), audience_of(origin)
    if r is None or o is None:
        return False
    o = set(json.loads(o))
    return "*" in o or set(json.loads(r)) <= o


def passes(row, round_value, session):
    """One reader's verdict on one row. With a declared round it is the gate;
    without one, only a row of the running session that declares no round
    either (or names `*`) passes -- the window and the handover keep a
    round-less conversation going and show nothing from elsewhere (OR-BD-4).
    A row of a declared round never reaches a call nobody declared a round
    for, though it stands in the same session (review M-7: the words of {e,b}
    reached a round-less call of that session, and a round-less recall took
    the addendum of an {e,a} gap). A row that names no session never passes
    a round-less read."""
    if audience_of(round_value) is None:
        if not session or str(row.get("session_id") or "") != session:
            return False
        own = audience_of(row.get("audience_set"))
        return own is not None and (own == "[]" or "*" in json.loads(own))
    return allowed(round_value, row.get("audience_set"))


ROUNDLESS = ["[]", "[\"*\"]"]


def round_where(round_value, session):
    """The store half of the audience gate (GH #932): the `where` terms a
    ledger read adds so that only rows this round may see come back -- page
    bounds, `scanned`, window and renewal sizes and turn counts then hang on
    visible rows alone, and a hidden row costs nothing a reader can count.
    With a declared, non-empty round it is `covers` (the affinity rule in the
    store). Without one -- or with a declared EMPTY round, which `covers`
    refuses -- only rows of the running session that declare no round either
    (`[]`, PP-BD-12) or name `*` come back; a row from before the rule (NULL)
    never does. None: nothing may be read at all (no round and no session).
    The Python gate below stays as the second line."""
    r = audience_of(round_value)
    if r is not None and r != "[]":
        return {"audience_set": {"covers": json.loads(r)}}
    if not session:
        return None
    return {"session_id": session, "audience_set": {"in": list(ROUNDLESS)}}


def audience_meet(values):
    """The audience of a row made of other rows (a summary, a handover
    block): the INTERSECTION of its sources, so it can never be wider than
    any of them (OR-BD-3). A source naming `*` is neutral; one source without
    an audience, or no source at all, makes the result None."""
    out, universal = None, False
    for v in values:
        c = audience_of(v)
        if c is None:
            return None
        s = set(json.loads(c))
        if "*" in s:
            universal = True
            continue
        out = s if out is None else out & s
    if out is None:
        return '["*"]' if universal else None
    return json.dumps(sorted(out), separators=(",", ":"))


FMT = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ"
# The five families an identity pusher may write (the pack lane of
# collector up to 4.4.1, GH #458/#488): a SUBSET of what a brain keeps durable.
# `identity_short` (GH #935) is the short form of `identity` a pusher may hand
# beside the full one: under the policy's `identity_budget` `split` the system
# part carries the short form and the full one rides once as a snapshot
# message, so a change of the identity no longer breaks the prompt cache.
PACK_SLOTS = ("identity", "identity_short", "persona", "handover", "instructions")
# THE SLOTS OF ONE SESSION (GH #925, review I-4). The collector writes these
# paths on EVERY assembly, empty included (collector README "THE seam", "The
# other side's words"): the legend of the channel (`roster`, `<ref> = <name>
# (<identity>)`), the open consultations (`consult`) and the peer rule
# (`instructions.peer`), and the advise mode (`instructions.mode`, the
# charter of a duplex call or "" -- set from the turn's own `context.engine`).
# They belong to the session of the call, not to the hive: kept in the
# hive-wide `slots`, an overlapping call of another session read them -- in a
# driver of two overlapping calls the {e,a} call carried the {e,b} call's
# legend, its consult and its peer rule, and 223 of 1 355 calls of a chat
# session carried the duplex charter of a voice call that ran beside it
# (review R2-I-1). So no lane writes them into `slots`; `in_curate` parks the
# call's own in its turn (`session_slots` of `pending:<call>`), and `./policy`
# takes them from there alone. Every call carries them whole, so nothing is
# lost.
SESSION_SLOTS = ("roster", "consult", "instructions.mode", "instructions.peer")
# The frames the collector puts in front of an advice and a delegation
# (collector `ADVICE_FRAME`, `DELEGATION_FRAME`). They arrive as user turns and
# are nobody's words, so they never become an episode.
ADVICE_PREFIX = "[advice from your reasoning core"
DELEGATION_PREFIX = "[delegation"
RECALL_TOOL = "memory_recall"
BRIEF_TOOL = "affinity_brief"
LANES = ("in_curate", "in_slots", "in_llm", "in_pack", "in_section", "in_pin", "in_addendum")
ME = "curator-intake"
FENCE = "```sidecar"
# THE CONTRACT'S OWN NOTHING-FORM (GH #871 I-1), for the sentence a model says
# beside a tool call. Such a sentence leaves the round as an interim answer and
# stands in every later window as an earlier answer; bare, it is the precedent
# #871 removed: replayed on 4 consult returns x 5, the block stood in 9 of 20
# answers on the return with the sentence bare and in 19 of 20 with this form
# beside it. One JSON object or empty (off, the default: a model behind a
# curator need not speak a sidecar at all); the value is the talky splitter's
# `nothing_block`, and an instance that runs one sets both.
_NB = str(P.get("nothing_block", "") or "").strip()
try:
    NOTHING_BLOCK = _NB if isinstance(json.loads(_NB or "null"), dict) else ""
except ValueError:
    sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: nothing_block is not one JSON object -- ignored\n")
    NOTHING_BLOCK = ""

# THE SECTIONS OF THE MODEL'S OWN BLOCK (GH #892, OR-KY-G2): the splitter cuts
# the block and hands `window` and `memory` here on `in_section` (`gap` is
# `./push`'s since GH #895: it marks a gap once and looks it up); this
# cell parses none of it beyond the keys it writes down. `memory` belongs to
# the memory hive and leaves again UNCHANGED on `sidecar` when this knob names
# it -- a talky's memory keeps its one door (R-27-2 Pkt. 6), a core that keeps
# no memory names nothing. What every section leaves in the ledger is a
# `marks` row: `topic` out of `memory`, `release`/`pin` out of `window`.
PASS_SECTIONS = [x.strip() for x in str(P.get("pass_sections", "") or "").split(",")
                 if x.strip()]
# The movements of a topic the memory section names (R-27-2 Pkt. 6).
TOPIC_MOVES = ("start", "continue", "end")
# `in_pin` (GH #892): what a pinning hive may name as its source -- one path
# segment of `pinned.<source>.<id>`, never the model's own -- and how long a
# pinned text may be (a system leaf holds 64 KiB; a pin is a line, not a file).
PIN_SOURCE_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_-"
PIN_MAX_CHARS = 16000
MODEL_SOURCE = "model"
# `replace_sources` (GH #916): the sources whose live pins end before the new
# ones are written -- each by the rule of a pin's `source`, at most this many.
# The bound keeps the one read of step A (`source in [...]`) a short list.
REPLACE_MAX_SOURCES = 16
# The tools with which a model asks back instead of answering (GH #925): the
# core's question to whoever asked it (`ask_requester`, GH #894) -- it could
# not go on without more from the person. Such a call ends the turn and never
# comes back as a round of this hive, so the `ask` mark is taken off the tap.
ASK_TOOLS = ("ask_requester",)
# THE FORM OF A `tool_error` VALUE (GH #925, OR-BD-6): `<tool>:<code>` reaches
# a judge as a sample, and a sample is never text -- a tool's refusal in its
# own words can carry a path, a name, the person's input. So a tool's name
# enters the value only when the tool stands in the menu (`tools.<name>` in
# `slots` or in the `system` tree of the same message) and in the form of a
# name (lower-case, digits, `_.-`, at most 64 characters), else `unknown`, and
# a code only in the NARROW form of
# a code: a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters and `_`, at most 32
# characters -- no digit, no dot, no `-` -- else `error`. A word with a dot is
# a file name (review m-5: `{"error": "report.txt"}` made
# `file.read:report.txt`); one with a digit or a `-` is a password, a card
# number, a name (review R2-I-2: `login:hunter2`, `pay:4111111111111111`,
# `file_read:secret-name`). Every code a shipped tool answers with is in
# that form (`not_found`, `no_such_file`, `rate_limited`, `missing_audience`).
CODE_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_.-"
CODE_MAX_CHARS = 64
ERROR_CODE_FIRST = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
ERROR_CODE_CHARS = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_"
ERROR_CODE_MAX_CHARS = 32
# What an `error` string says when there is none (compared stripped, in lower
# case): such a result is no failure (review I-5).
NO_ERROR = ("none", "null", "false")
# THE ROUND (GH #925, OR-BD.A.1): the audience of the message this step
# serves, read afresh in every step -- a store answer carries the context of
# the lane message that caused it. Every `wall`, `marks` and `pins` row this
# cell writes carries it. A round that declares none writes `[]` (PP-BD-12),
# never NULL: the store filter (`round_where`) hands a round-less read exactly
# the rows of its session that say `[]` or `*`, and NULL is left to the rows
# from before the rule, which no reader takes.
ROUND = ctx.get("audience_set")
AUDIENCE = audience_of(ROUND)
# The audience a row of this step is written with and the turn index is
# counted under (GH #932, OR-S3.K.1): the round, or `[]` without one.
ROW_AUDIENCE = AUDIENCE if AUDIENCE is not None else "[]"

try:
    _MEM
except NameError:
    # A cache of this child's own writes, never the truth (`code` runner mode
    # `resident`): a restarted child starts empty and the ledger read decides.
    _MEM = {"seq": 0, "wall": set(), "blocks": set(), "episode": {}}


def canonical(value):
    """The one serialisation a block is hashed and stored in: keys sorted,
    UTF-8, no whitespace."""
    return json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)


def block_hash(value):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(value).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def block_span(text):
    """Where an answer's sidecar block stands: (start, end) or None.

    The boundary is the fence `talky/splitter` cuts (GH #379, #605): the
    ```sidecar fence, or the legacy ```memory fence, to the next closing fence
    or to the end of the text when the completion stopped inside the block.
    Measured, never parsed -- the sections inside are somebody else's business.
    """
    low = text.lower()
    for fence in ("```sidecar", "```memory"):
        at = low.find(fence)
        if at < 0:
            continue
        head = text.find("\n", at)
        close = text.find("```", head + 1) if head >= 0 else -1
        if head >= 0 and close >= 0:
            return at, close + 3
        return at, len(text)
    return None


def stripped_text(text):
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return text
    return (text[:span[0]] + text[span[1]:]).strip()


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime(FMT)


def next_seq(n):
    """`n` fresh wall sequence numbers: microseconds since the epoch, strictly
    above anything this child minted before. The store has no autoincrement, and
    this cell is the wall's only writer, so a clock reading made strictly
    monotonic here is the order of arrival."""
    base = int(datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).timestamp() * 1000000)
    base = max(base, _MEM["seq"] + 1)
    _MEM["seq"] = base + n - 1
    return [base + i for i in range(n)]


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def park(reason=""):
    if reason:
        sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: %s\n" % reason)
    emit([])


def lstore(ops, phase, reply=ME, call="", reason=""):
    """One message to `./ledger`. Every key the edge reads is always present
    (a failed CEL modifier skips the edge)."""
    return {"header": {"route": "lstore", "phase": phase, "reply_cell": reply,
                       "cur_call": call, "cur_reason": reason},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in ops]}


def legs(body):
    """The answer of a store message by tool_call id: payload, error code and
    rows affected -- for a bundle (`results[]`) and for a single op alike."""
    out = {}
    msgs = body.get("messages") or []
    results = body.get("results")
    for m in msgs:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "null")
        except Exception:
            payload = None
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = {"payload": payload, "error_code": "",
                                       "rows_affected": 0}
    if isinstance(results, list):
        for r in results:
            if not isinstance(r, dict):
                continue
            leg = out.setdefault(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or ""),
                                 {"payload": None, "error_code": "", "rows_affected": 0})
            leg["error_code"] = str(r.get("error_code") or "")
            leg["rows_affected"] = int(r.get("rows_affected") or 0)
    elif len(out) == 1:
        leg = next(iter(out.values()))
        leg["error_code"] = str(hop.get("error_code") or "")
        leg["rows_affected"] = int(hop.get("rows_affected") or 0)
    return out


def rows(lg, cid):
    p = (lg.get(cid) or {}).get("payload")
    return p if isinstance(p, list) else []


def sel(table, columns, where=None, order=None, limit=None):
    a = {"operation": "select", "table": table, "columns": columns}
    if where:
        a["where"] = where
    if order:
        a["order_by"] = [{"col": c, "dir": o} for c, o in order]
    if limit:
        a["limit"] = limit
    return a


def ins(table, row):
    return {"operation": "insert", "table": table, "row": row}


def audienced(row):
    """A row of `wall`, `marks` or `pins` with the round's audience (GH #925).
    Without one it is `[]` (PP-BD-12), never NULL: such a row belongs to the
    round-less conversation of its own session -- `round_where` hands it to
    that and to nothing else -- while NULL stays the mark of a row from before
    the rule, which no reader takes (OR-BD-5)."""
    row["audience_set"] = ROW_AUDIENCE
    return row


def with_round(cid, table, columns, where=None, order=None, limit=None, session=None):
    """One ledger read for the round (GH #932): `where` with `round_where`
    merged in, or None when the round may read nothing at all (no round and
    no session) -- the read is then left out and its rows are empty, without
    a store call. `summaries` and `pins` name no session, so they pass None."""
    rw = round_where(ROUND, session)
    if rw is None:
        return None
    return (cid, sel(table, columns, dict(where or {}, **rw), order, limit))


def marks_read(session, turn):
    """The marks a round already left, read in step A: `(kind, value)` is the
    key a mark of a section or of the tap is written by once."""
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "a-marks",
            "text": json.dumps(sel("marks", ["kind", "value"],
                                   {"session_id": session, "turn_id": turn}))}


def mark_ops(pfx, session, turn, pairs, stamp):
    """One `marks` insert per `(kind, value)`, in order."""
    ops = []
    for (k, v), seq in zip(pairs, next_seq(len(pairs)) if pairs else []):
        ops.append(("%s-%d" % (pfx, seq), ins("marks", audienced({
            "seq": seq, "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn, "kind": k, "value": v,
            "at": stamp}))))
    return ops


def code_form(value, chars=CODE_CHARS):
    """`value` stripped when it is in the form of a code (`chars`, at most
    CODE_MAX_CHARS), else "" -- the one gate a tool's name and a code pass on
    their way into a `tool_error` value (GH #925, OR-BD-6: never text)."""
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    return s if 0 < len(s) <= CODE_MAX_CHARS and all(c in chars for c in s) else ""


def error_code(value):
    """The code half of a `tool_error` value: `[a-z][a-z_]{0,31}` (review
    m-5, R2-I-2), else ""."""
    s = str(value or "").strip()
    return s if 0 < len(s) <= ERROR_CODE_MAX_CHARS and s[0] in ERROR_CODE_FIRST \
        and all(c in ERROR_CODE_CHARS for c in s) else ""


def tool_failure(el):
    """`(failed, code)` of one `tool_result` turn (GH #925). A tool says it
    failed on the turn (`finish_reason` "error", an `error_code`) or in its
    text, in the forms the shipped tools answer in: `{"error": "<code>", ...}`
    (the curator's history tools), `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", ...}}` (the
    file tools), a bare `ok: false` or an `error_code`. A refusal a tool says
    only on its hop never reaches a round, and prose is no failure. Every
    place counts as a failure whatever it says; the code is the first of them
    in the narrow form of a code (`error_code`; "" when none is -- a sentence
    is no code, OR-BD-6, a file name is none, review m-5, nor a word with a
    digit or a `-`, review R2-I-2). An
    `error` string that says there is none (NO_ERROR) is no failure."""
    raw = str(el.get("error_code") or "").strip()
    failed = bool(raw) or str(el.get("finish_reason") or "") == "error"
    code = error_code(raw)
    try:
        body = json.loads(str(el.get("text") or ""))
    except ValueError:
        body = None
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        err = body.get("error")
        if isinstance(err, str) and err.strip() and err.strip().lower() not in NO_ERROR:
            failed, code = True, code or error_code(err)
        elif isinstance(err, dict) and err:
            failed, code = True, code or error_code(err.get("code"))
        if body.get("ok") is False:
            failed = True
        own = body.get("error_code")
        if isinstance(own, str) and own.strip():
            failed, code = True, code or error_code(own)
    return failed, code


def sidecar_sections(text):
    """The sections of an answer's ```sidecar block: the one JSON object
    between the fence line and the closing fence, its top-level keys the
    sections (the talky splitter's grammar, GH #605) -- or {} when there is
    none that reads. The legacy ```memory fence is the single section
    `memory` and names no other."""
    span = block_span(text)
    if span is None:
        return {}
    block = text[span[0]:span[1]]
    head = block.find("\n")
    if head < 0 or not block.lower().startswith(FENCE):
        return {}
    inner = block[head + 1:]
    if inner.endswith("```"):
        inner = inner[:-3]
    try:
        parsed = json.loads(inner.strip())
    except ValueError:
        return {}
    return parsed if isinstance(parsed, dict) else {}


def has_words(payload):
    """A section that says something: text that is not blank, or an object
    that is not empty -- the splitter hands no section without words on."""
    if isinstance(payload, str):
        return bool(payload.strip())
    return isinstance(payload, dict) and bool(payload)


def tap_marks(messages, finish):
    """The marks the model's own output leaves (GH #925), each `(kind,
    value)` once: `ask` for a call of an ASK_TOOLS tool, and `correction`
    when the block of a final answer carries that section. What is counted is
    the model rewriting a standing instruction (the core's advice to rewrite
    one), NOT a person correcting the model (OR-BD-17): that one says nothing
    in a block."""
    out = []
    for m in messages:
        if m.get("origin") == "assistant" and m.get("type") == "tool_call":
            name = tool_name(m)
            if name in ASK_TOOLS and ("ask", name) not in out:
                out.append(("ask", name))
    if finish in ("stop", "length"):
        for m in messages:
            if m.get("origin") != "assistant" or m.get("type") != "text":
                continue
            if has_words(sidecar_sections(str(m.get("text") or "")).get("correction")) \
                    and ("correction", "") not in out:
                out.append(("correction", ""))
    return out


def tool_name(el):
    try:
        return str((json.loads(el.get("text") or "{}") or {}).get("name") or "")
    except Exception:
        return ""


def kinds_of(elements):
    """The ledger kind of each element of a round, in order."""
    recall_ids, brief_ids = set(), set()
    for el in elements:
        if el.get("origin") == "assistant" and el.get("type") == "tool_call":
            name = tool_name(el)
            if name == RECALL_TOOL:
                recall_ids.add(str(el.get("id") or ""))
            elif name == BRIEF_TOOL:
                brief_ids.add(str(el.get("id") or ""))
    out = []
    for el in elements:
        origin, typ = el.get("origin"), el.get("type")
        eid = str(el.get("id") or "")
        text = str(el.get("text") or "")
        if typ == "tool_call":
            out.append("recall" if eid in recall_ids else
                       "brief" if eid in brief_ids else "tool_call")
        elif typ == "tool_result":
            out.append("recall" if eid in recall_ids else
                       "brief" if eid in brief_ids else "tool_result")
        elif origin == "peer":
            out.append("peer")
        elif origin == "assistant":
            out.append("assistant")
        elif origin == "user" and text.startswith(ADVICE_PREFIX):
            out.append("advice")
        elif origin == "user" and text.startswith(DELEGATION_PREFIX):
            out.append("delegation")
        else:
            out.append("user")
    return out


def with_nth(elements):
    """(element, hash, nth): nth counts the earlier copies of the same hash in
    the round, so the same round sent again maps onto the same keys (OR-KX-K3)."""
    seen, out = {}, []
    for el in elements:
        h = block_hash(el)
        n = seen.get(h, 0)
        seen[h] = n + 1
        out.append((el, h, n))
    return out


def leaves_of(tree, prefix=""):
    """The (path, text) leaves of a `system` tree and its `$replace` roots, read
    the way the `llm` cell reads them: an object with `text` is a leaf, `$`-keys
    are markers, anything that is not an object is nothing."""
    leaves, roots = [], []
    if not isinstance(tree, dict):
        return leaves, roots
    if tree.get("$replace") is True:
        roots.append(prefix)
    if "text" in tree and prefix:
        leaves.append((prefix, str(tree.get("text") or "")))
        return leaves, roots
    for k in sorted(tree):
        if k.startswith("$"):
            continue
        path = k if not prefix else prefix + "." + k
        lv, rt = leaves_of(tree[k], path)
        leaves += lv
        roots += rt
    return leaves, roots


def slot_element(path, text):
    return {"path": path, "text": text}


def session_bound(path):
    """Whether `path` is a slot of one session (SESSION_SLOTS, review I-4):
    the path itself or one below it."""
    return any(path == p or path.startswith(p + ".") for p in SESSION_SLOTS)


def session_leaves(system):
    """The leaves of a session's own slots in one `system` tree, as sorted
    `[path, text]` pairs -- what a call parks beside its turn (review I-4)."""
    return sorted([p, t] for p, t in leaves_of(system)[0] if session_bound(p))


def slot_ops(current, system, owner, stamp, pfx):
    """Blocks and slot writes for one incoming `system` tree.

    The collector wins at its own leaf paths: a pack leaf on a path the
    collector holds is not written. A `$replace` root drops this owner's rows
    below it that the tree no longer names -- never another owner's.
    A slot of one session (`session_bound`) is never written here, and a row
    under one that a ledger from before review I-4 still holds is deleted
    in the same bundle, whoever wrote it: no reader takes it any more."""
    leaves, roots = leaves_of(system)
    have = {str(r.get("path") or ""): r for r in current}
    stale = sorted(p for p in have if session_bound(p))
    blocks, ops, named = [], [], set()
    for i, (path, text) in enumerate(leaves):
        if session_bound(path):
            continue
        el = slot_element(path, text)
        h = block_hash(el)
        blocks.append((el, h, "system"))
        named.add(path)
        row = have.get(path)
        if row is not None:
            if str(row.get("owner") or "") == "collector" and owner == "pack":
                continue
            if str(row.get("hash") or "") == h and str(row.get("owner") or "") == owner:
                continue
            ops.append(("%s-su%d" % (pfx, i), {"operation": "update", "table": "slots",
                        "set": {"hash": h, "owner": owner, "at": stamp},
                        "where": {"path": path}}))
        else:
            ops.append(("%s-si%d" % (pfx, i), ins("slots", {"path": path, "hash": h,
                                                            "owner": owner, "at": stamp})))
    gone = []
    for root in roots:
        for path, row in have.items():
            if str(row.get("owner") or "") != owner or path in named or path in gone \
                    or path in stale:
                continue
            if root == "" or path == root or path.startswith(root + "."):
                gone.append(path)
    if gone:
        ops.append(("%s-sd" % pfx, {"operation": "delete", "table": "slots",
                    "where": {"path": {"in": sorted(gone)}, "owner": owner}}))
    if stale:
        ops.append(("%s-ss" % pfx, {"operation": "delete", "table": "slots",
                    "where": {"path": {"in": stale}}}))
    return blocks, ops


def block_ops(items, have, stamp, pfx):
    """Inserts for the blocks not yet in the ledger, each hash once."""
    ops, done = [], set(have) | _MEM["blocks"]
    for i, (el, h, kind) in enumerate(items):
        if h in done:
            continue
        done.add(h)
        _MEM["blocks"].add(h)
        body = canonical(el)
        ops.append(("%s-b%d" % (pfx, i), ins("blocks", {
            "hash": h, "kind": kind, "chars": len(str(el.get("text") or "")),
            "body": body, "first_seen": stamp})))
    return ops


def pending_key(pid):
    return "pending:" + pid


def plan_cover(plan, cover_rows):
    """Where the window's wall starts: the cover of the current plan, or --
    in a ledger that has none yet -- the newest summary's `covers_to_seq`."""
    if isinstance(plan, dict) and plan.get("cover") is not None:
        try:
            return int(plan.get("cover") or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    return int((cover_rows[0].get("covers_to_seq") or 0) if cover_rows else 0)


def norm_id(value):
    """A block id as a model writes it -- `#0123456789ab`, `[#0123...]`,
    bare -- as its 12 hex digits, or "" when it is none."""
    s = str(value or "").strip().strip("[]").strip().lstrip("#").strip().lower()
    s = s[:12]
    if len(s) != 12 or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in s):
        return ""
    return s


def section_marks(section, payload):
    """The `marks` rows `(kind, value)` one section leaves, in the order they
    are written: in a `window` section the releases before the pins, so a pin
    of the same id in the same block is the later word (review focus 2)."""
    payload = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
    if section == "memory":
        # OR-KY-71: the mark carries the topic's name beside its movement, as
        # canonical JSON like the `gap` mark -- a reader of the ledger (the
        # handover, the push) has to know WHICH topic is open, not only that
        # one moved. `name` is "" when the section names none.
        topic = payload.get("topic") if isinstance(payload.get("topic"), dict) else {}
        move = str(topic.get("movement") or "").strip().lower()
        if move not in TOPIC_MOVES:
            return []
        name = str(topic.get("name") or "").strip()
        return [("topic", canonical({"movement": move, "name": name}))]
    if section == "window":
        out = []
        for kind in ("release", "pin"):
            items = payload.get(kind)
            items = items if isinstance(items, list) else ([items] if items else [])
            for item in items:
                mid = norm_id(item)
                if mid:
                    out.append((kind, mid))
                else:
                    sys.stderr.write("curator/intake: window %s %r is not a block id"
                                     " -- ignored\n" % (kind, item))
        return out
    return []


def source_ok(source):
    """A pinning hive's name: one path segment of `pinned.<source>.<id>`,
    never the model's own."""
    return bool(source) and source != MODEL_SOURCE and len(source) <= 64 \
        and all(c in PIN_SOURCE_CHARS for c in source)


def replace_of(body):
    """`replace_sources` of an `in_pin` body as (sources, reason). Absent is
    ([], ""); anything malformed refuses the whole message (reason set): a
    replacement half understood would end the wrong pins or keep stale ones."""
    if "replace_sources" not in body:
        return [], ""
    raw = body.get("replace_sources")
    if not isinstance(raw, list):
        return [], "replace_sources is not a list"
    if len(raw) > REPLACE_MAX_SOURCES:
        return [], "replace_sources names %d sources, over %d" % (len(raw), REPLACE_MAX_SOURCES)
    out = []
    for s in raw:
        if not isinstance(s, str) or not source_ok(s):
            return [], "replace_sources: %r is no pinning hive's name" % (s,)
        if s not in out:
            out.append(s)
    return out, ""


def pin_live(until, as_of):
    """Whether a `pins` row still stands at `as_of` (an aware datetime): no
    `until`, or one that does not read as a time, stands for ever -- the rule
    `./handover` `pin_valid` and `./policy` `pin_split` read it by."""
    u = str(until or "").strip()
    if not u:
        return True
    try:
        t = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(u.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
    except ValueError:
        return True
    if t.tzinfo is None:
        t = t.replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    return t > as_of


def pin_of(p, stamp):
    """One pin of `in_pin` as (element, row), or a reason it is refused."""
    if not isinstance(p, dict):
        return None, "a pin is an object"
    text = str(p.get("text") or "")
    source = str(p.get("source") or "")
    until = str(p.get("until") or "").strip()
    if not text.strip():
        return None, "a pin without text"
    if len(text) > PIN_MAX_CHARS:
        return None, "a pin of %d characters, over %d" % (len(text), PIN_MAX_CHARS)
    if not source_ok(source):
        return None, "source %r is no pinning hive's name" % source
    if until:
        try:
            datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(until.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        except ValueError:
            return None, "until %r is no RFC 3339 time" % until
    el = {"type": "pin", "source": source, "text": text}
    return el, {"hash": block_hash(el), "source": source, "until": until, "at": stamp}

def episode_turn_id(session, audience, index):
    """The id `./writer` gives an episode on `turn_write`, `<session>#<tag>-<index>`
    (GH #932) -- the same code, locked equal by gh941: the model call names the
    person's episode of its turn by it (GH #941), so whoever reads a section of
    the answer addresses that episode without building the id itself."""
    tag = hashlib.sha256(audience.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return "%s#%s-%d" % (session, tag, index)


def stage_a(pid, stash, hashes, session="", turn="", cover=False, slots=False):
    """Step A: park the payload, read what is there -- one bundle."""
    ops = [("a-put", ins("state", {"key": pending_key(pid), "value": canonical(stash)})),
           ("a-echo", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": pending_key(pid)}))]
    if slots:
        ops.append(("a-slots", sel("slots", ["path", "hash", "owner"])))
    if hashes:
        ops.append(("a-blocks", sel("blocks", ["hash"], {"hash": {"in": sorted(set(hashes))}})))
    if session:
        # Dedupe by key, unfiltered: the round's own rows of this turn, read to
        # write nothing twice (a turn is one round's).
        ops.append(("a-wall", sel("wall", ["hash", "nth"],
                                  {"session_id": session, "turn_id": turn})))
        # The last turn index of THIS round of the session (OR-S3.K.1): counted
        # over every round, the index a writer stamps into `turn_id` told a
        # round how many turns it did not see. Exact audience, so a `*` row or
        # one of a wider round is not counted -- each round counts from 0.
        ops.append(("a-epi", sel("wall", ["episode_idx"],
                                 {"session_id": session, "audience_set": ROW_AUDIENCE,
                                  "episode_idx": {"is_null": False}},
                                 [("episode_idx", "desc")], 1)))
        # The person's latest episode of THIS round of the session (GH #941):
        # the model call names it, so every sidecar section of the answer can
        # address it. A call that writes no person row -- a tool round, a
        # consult's advice coming back under a turn id of its own -- answers
        # the person's words that row holds. Exact audience, like the index.
        ops.append(("a-said", sel("wall", ["episode_idx"],
                                  {"session_id": session, "audience_set": ROW_AUDIENCE,
                                   "kind": {"in": ["user", "peer"]},
                                   "episode_idx": {"is_null": False}},
                                  [("episode_idx", "desc")], 1)))
    if cover:
        read = with_round("a-cover", "summaries", ["covers_to_seq"], None,
                          [("covers_to_seq", "desc")], 1)
        if read:
            ops.append(read)
        ops.append(("a-plan", sel("state", ["key", "value"], {"key": "window_plan"})))
    return lstore(ops, "a", ME, pid, stash.get("lane", ""))

    # By hash: its `until` and its audience (GH #925), each as the door
    # writes it, so "the same again" compares like with like.
    pinned = {str(r.get("hash") or ""): (str(r.get("until") or ""),
                                         audience_of(r.get("audience_set")))
              for r in rows(lg, "a-pins")}
    items = []
    # `replace_sources` (GH #916): every live pin of the named sources ends
    # now -- `until` set, no row deleted -- EXCEPT one the new set carries: a
    # live hash pinned again stays alive (ending it first and then finding
    # "same text, same until, nothing to do" below would leave it dead). A hash
    # whose row already ended lives again through the `until` update below.
    keep = {str((p.get("row") or {}).get("hash") or "") for p in (stash.get("pins") or [])}
    as_of = datetime.datetime.strptime(stamp, FMT).replace(tzinfo=datetime.timezone.utc)
    ending = sorted({str(r.get("hash") or "") for r in rows(lg, "a-live")
                     if str(r.get("hash") or "") not in keep
                     and pin_live(r.get("until"), as_of)} - {""})
    if ending:
        ops.append(("bp-end", {"operation": "update", "table": "pins",
                               "set": {"until": stamp},
                               "where": {"hash": {"in": ending}}}))
    for i, p in enumerate(stash.get("pins") or []):
        row = p.get("row") or {}
        h = str(row.get("hash") or "")
        items.append((p.get("element") or {}, h, "pin"))
        until = str(row.get("until") or "")
        if h not in pinned:
            ops.append(("bp-i%d" % i, ins("pins", audienced(dict(row)))))
        elif pinned[h] != (until, AUDIENCE):
            # The same text pinned again: a new `until`, never a new place --
            # and the round of THIS pin (OR-BD.A.3): the latest door decides
            # who the pin stands for, as it decides how long.
            ops.append(("bp-u%d" % i, {"operation": "update", "table": "pins",
                                       "set": audienced({"until": until}),
                                       "where": {"hash": h}}))
    ops += block_ops(items, have_blocks, stamp, "bp")

# -- slots (collector / pack) ---------------------------------------------
if kind_lane in ("in_curate", "in_slots", "in_pack"):
    sblocks, sops = slot_ops(current_slots, stash.get("system") or {},
                             str(stash.get("owner") or "collector"), stamp, "b")
    ops += block_ops(sblocks, have_blocks, stamp, "bs")
    ops += sops

# -- wall rows (curate / tap) ----------------------------------------------
episodes = []
if kind_lane in ("in_curate", "in_llm", "in_addendum"):
    session, turn = str(stash.get("session") or ""), str(stash.get("turn") or "")
    try:
        it = int(str(stash.get("iter") or "0"))
    except ValueError:
        it = 0
    elements = [m for m in (stash.get("messages") or []) if isinstance(m, dict)]
    triples = with_nth(elements)
    if kind_lane == "in_llm":
        kinds = ["assistant"] * len(elements)
        finals = [int(stash.get("final") or 0)] * len(elements)
    else:
        kinds = kinds_of(elements)
        # A round without a tool call that carries the agent's own words is a
        # turn cut on the model's clock (duplex voice, R-25-9): its answer half
        # is said, final, and an episode -- that model is not behind the tap.
        # Beside a tool call the same shape is prose on the way to a call. The
        # evidence pairs a collector hangs on every round (recall, brief) are
        # no call of the model's: counted, they kept every duplex answer half
        # of the shipped surface (talky `memory_tier` "1") out of the episodes
        # (review I-1).
        calls = any(k == "tool_call" for k in kinds)
        finals = [1 if k == "assistant" and not calls else 0 for k in kinds]
    items = [(el, h, k) for (el, h, _), k in zip(triples, kinds)]
    for (el, _, _), k, f in zip(triples, kinds, finals):
        if k == "assistant" and f:
            # The answer without its block is a block too: the window shows it
            # that way when the block is over `sidecar_max_chars` (GH #871), and
            # a call record names only blocks the ledger holds.
            bare = dict(el, text=stripped_text(str(el.get("text") or "")))
            items.append((bare, block_hash(bare), "assistant"))
    ops += block_ops(items, have_blocks, stamp, "bw")
    have_wall = {(str(r.get("hash") or ""), int(r.get("nth") or 0))
                 for r in rows(lg, "a-wall")}
    epi = rows(lg, "a-epi")
    last_idx = int(epi[0].get("episode_idx")) if epi and epi[0].get("episode_idx") is not None else -1
    # Keyed by (session, audience) like the read above (OR-S3.K.1).
    last_idx = max(last_idx, _MEM["episode"].get((session, ROW_AUDIENCE), -1))
    fresh = []
    for (el, h, n), k, final in zip(triples, kinds, finals):
        key = (session, turn, h, n)
        if (h, n) in have_wall or key in _MEM["wall"]:
            continue
        if k == "assistant" and not str(el.get("text") or ""):
            # An empty answer half says nothing and is refused by providers.
            continue
        fresh.append((el, h, n, k, final))
    seqs = next_seq(len(fresh)) if fresh else []
    for (el, h, n, k, final), seq in zip(fresh, seqs):
        _MEM["wall"].add((session, turn, h, n))
        idx = None
        if k in ("user", "peer") or (k == "assistant" and final):
            last_idx += 1
            idx = last_idx
            text = str(el.get("text") or "")
            # `audience`: the round the index counts in -- `./writer` makes it
            # part of the turn id, so two rounds of one session never collide.
            ep = {"session_id": session, "index": idx, "iter": str(it), "at": stamp,
                  "role": k, "text": stripped_text(text) if k == "assistant" else text,
                  "audience": ROW_AUDIENCE}
            if k == "peer":
                ep["speaker"] = str(el.get("speaker") or "")
                ep["speaker_ref"] = str(el.get("speaker_ref") or "")
            episodes.append(ep)
        ops.append(("bw-w%d" % seq, ins("wall", audienced({
            "seq": seq, "session_id": session, "turn_id": turn, "iter": it, "kind": k,
            "hash": h, "nth": n, "final": final, "episode_idx": idx, "at": stamp}))))
    if last_idx >= 0:
        _MEM["episode"][(session, ROW_AUDIENCE)] = last_idx
    if kind_lane == "in_curate":
        # GH #925: a tool that failed, once per result -- only a result written
        # as a new wall row now marks, so the wall's own key (and `_MEM`) makes
        # the mark exactly once. The tool's name is the call's of the same id
        # in the round, in code form or `unknown` (a name is the model's words
        # too, OR-BD-6); an evidence pair is `recall`/`brief`, never counted.
        # A name the menu does not hold is `unknown` as well (OR-BD-92): a
        # model can make one up out of the person's words in the form of a
        # name -- `lookup.alice-smith`, `my-secret` reached a judge as samples
        # (review of fix round 3, m5.py). The menu is what `slots` held before
        # this message (step A read it) and what its own `system` tree brings:
        # the call was made from the one, the result may come with the other.
        menu = {p[6:] for p in [str(r.get("path") or "") for r in current_slots]
                + [p for p, _ in leaves_of(stash.get("system") or {})[0]]
                if p.startswith("tools.")}
        names = {str(el.get("id") or ""): tool_name(el) for el in elements
                 if el.get("origin") == "assistant" and el.get("type") == "tool_call"}
        failed = []
        for el, _, _, k, _ in fresh:
            if k != "tool_result":
                continue
            bad, code = tool_failure(el)
            if bad:
                name = names.get(str(el.get("id") or "")) or ""
                name = (code_form(name) if name in menu else "") or "unknown"
                failed.append(("tool_error", "%s:%s" % (name, code or "error")))
        ops += mark_ops("bw-m", session, turn, failed, stamp)

# -- marks of the model's own output (the tap, GH #925) -------------------
if kind_lane == "in_llm":
    said_now = [(k, v) for k, v in (tuple(m) for m in (stash.get("marks") or []))
                if (k, v) not in have_marks]
    ops += mark_ops("bk", str(stash.get("session") or ""), str(stash.get("turn") or ""),
                    said_now, stamp)

if episodes:
    out.append({"header": {"route": "episode"}, "messages": [], "episodes": episodes})

if kind_lane == "in_curate":
    # The plan of the window (GH #892): which rows the next call shows, fixed
    # between two rebuilds. It rides in the parked turn, so `./policy` renders
    # exactly the plan the rows below were read for.
    plan_text = str(((rows(lg, "a-plan") or [{}])[0]).get("value") or "")
    try:
        plan = json.loads(plan_text) if plan_text else {}
    except ValueError:
        plan = {}
    plan = plan if isinstance(plan, dict) else {}
    cover = plan_cover(plan, rows(lg, "a-cover"))
    keep = [int(s) for s in (plan.get("keep") or []) if str(s).lstrip("-").isdigit()]
    slim = {k: stash.get(k) for k in ("lane", "session", "turn", "iter", "hop")}
    # The person's episode of this turn, by the id `./writer` gives it (GH
    # #941): `./policy` hands the parked hop on with the model call, the brain
    # edge promotes it to `context.episode_turn_id`, and every sidecar section
    # of the answer carries it -- before, a section carried only the round's
    # uuid and a reader could not address the episode (`in_affect` with
    # `session_id` + `turn_id`) without minting the id itself. A fresh person
    # row of this call counts, else the latest one of the round in the session
    # (a tool round or a consult's advice answers it); a session without one
    # names none, and a value a caller put on the hop never passes.
    said_idx = [ep["index"] for ep in episodes if ep.get("role") in ("user", "peer")]
    for row in rows(lg, "a-said"):
        if str(row.get("episode_idx") if row.get("episode_idx") is not None else "").isdigit():
            said_idx.append(int(row.get("episode_idx")))
    hop_on = {k: v for k, v in dict(stash.get("hop") or {}).items() if k != "episode_turn_id"}
    if said_idx:
        hop_on["episode_turn_id"] = episode_turn_id(session, ROW_AUDIENCE, max(said_idx))
    slim["hop"] = hop_on
    slim["plan"] = plan_text if plan else ""
    if "tool_scope" in stash:
        slim["tool_scope"] = stash.get("tool_scope")
    # The slots of this call's session (review I-4): parked with its turn, the
    # one place `./policy` takes them from -- complete, because the collector
    # writes each of them on every assembly, empty included.
    slim["session_slots"] = session_leaves(stash.get("system") or {})
    ops.append(("b-slim", {"operation": "update", "table": "state",
                           "set": {"value": canonical(slim)},
                           "where": {"key": pending_key(pid)}}))
    ops.append(("b-slimq", sel("state", ["value"], {"key": pending_key(pid)})))
    # The hashes `./policy` fetches for the window (GH #932): only rows this
    # round may see, so the number of blocks fetched says nothing about
    # another round's. `slots` carry no audience and stay whole.
    wsess = str(stash.get("session") or "")
    reads = [with_round("b-wallh", "wall", ["hash"], {"seq": {"gt": cover}}, session=wsess)]
    if keep:
        reads.append(with_round("b-keeph", "wall", ["hash"], {"seq": {"in": keep}},
                                session=wsess))
    reads.append(("b-slotsh", sel("slots", ["hash"])))
    reads.append(with_round("b-pins", "pins", ["hash"]))
    reads.append(with_round("b-cover", "summaries", ["covers_to_seq"], None,
                            [("covers_to_seq", "desc")], 1))
    ops += [r for r in reads if r]
    out.insert(0, lstore(ops, "win-hashes", "curator-policy", pid, ""))
    emit(out)

if kind_lane == "in_llm":
    call = str(stash.get("call") or "")
    ops.append(("b-state", sel("state", ["key", "value"],
                               {"key": {"in": [pending_key(pid), "armed_call", "last_call"]}})))
    ops.append(("b-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                           "where": {"key": pending_key(pid)}}))
    out.insert(0, lstore(ops, "tap", "curator-policy", call, ""))
    emit(out)

ops.append(("b-drop", {"operation": "delete", "table": "state",
                       "where": {"key": pending_key(pid)}}))
out.insert(0, lstore(ops, "done", ME, pid, ""))
emit(out)

nothing_block.description: The contract's nothing-form for the sentence a model says beside a tool call (GH #871 I-1): one JSON object, rendered as a sidecar fence after such a sentence when it carries no block of its own, so the sentence stands in later windows with a precedent. Empty (the default) = off. A talky runs the value of its splitter's `nothing_block`.

pass_sections.description: The sections of the model's sidecar block that leave the hive again UNCHANGED on `sidecar` after their mark is written, comma-separated (GH #892): a talky names `memory`, so its memory keeps the one door it has (R-27-2 Pkt. 6); a core that keeps no memory names nothing. Empty (the default) = none.

description.purpose: The one writer of the wall: every element that enters the model's window -- a turn of the running round, the model's final answer off the tap, a durable system slot, a gap's find `./push` kept for the next round -- becomes a block (once per hash) and a wall row (once per session, turn, hash and copy); a section of the model's sidecar block becomes `marks` rows, a pin of another hive a block of kind `pin` and a `pins` row. Two steps per message against the ledger: park the payload and read what is there in one bundle, then write only what is new.
description.not_in_scope: No window, no model call, no episode shape: it hands the window to `./policy` and the participant turns to `./writer`.
description.emits_meaning: lstore: ledger operations (`hop.phase`, `hop.reply_cell` say who reads the answer). episode: the participant turns just written, for `./writer`. pack_ack: the receipt of a pack. sidecar: a section named in `pass_sections`, unchanged, back on the route it came out of the splitter on.
description.consumes_meaning: The seven lanes in_curate, in_slots, in_llm, in_pack, in_section, in_pin and in_addendum (from `./push`: a gap's find as a `memory_recall` pair, for the round it opens), and the ledger's answers to its own two steps.
